title: Ordinary right adjoints reindex coherent colimit cocones
statement:
Use nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, right-pinched mapping spaces and colimiting cocones as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I,J$ be small ordinary categories in a fixed universe, and let $L:J\to I$ and $R:I\to J$ be ordinary functors with an adjunction $L\dashv R$, meaning bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_I(Lj,i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_J(j,Ri)$ natural in $i,j$. Let $\mathcal E$ be any quasicategory in a sufficiently large universe, $p:N(J)\to\mathcal E$ a coherent diagram, and $e\in\mathcal E$. Restriction along $N(R)$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_J e)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(p\circ N(R),\Delta_I e),$$
where $\Delta_J e$ and $\Delta_I e$ denote the constant diagrams. This is the restriction map itself and is natural in $p$ and $e$. Consequently, for any coherent cocone $a:p\to\Delta_J c$, the cocone $a$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $N(R)$ is colimiting, with the same vertex $c$. No existence of any other colimits in $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Propositions 4.1.1.7-8, printed pp. 226 and 236-238: specialize to the nerve of an ordinary right adjoint; the comma category j/R has initial object (Lj,unit_j). Fixed-vertex cocone spaces are the fibers in Proposition 4.1.1.7, expressed in the coherent comma convention of the definition node. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.
